issue_title: autocall full behavior change in 8.27 (not present in 8.26.)
issue_body:
In 8.26 autocall of full checked for `__call__` on the object (I believe). Seems in 8.27 it is much more aggressive and will autocall for **everything**


```
In [17]: foo = dict()

In [18]: foo
-------> foo()
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[18], line 1
----> 1 foo()

TypeError: 'dict' object is not callable

In [19]:
```

Not sure if perhaps it is related to this PR #14486 or not

hints_text:
Can maybe this get a bug label just to help folks find that this is a known issue?
@krpatter-intc thanks for the report. I confirm the bug isn't there in 8.26 and appeared in 8.27. Minimal reproducible example requires setting autocall to full

```
In [1]: %autocall 2
Automatic calling is: Full

In [2]: foo = dict()

In [3]: foo
------> foo()
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[3], line 1
----> 1 foo()

TypeError: 'dict' object is not callable
```

I left a comment on the PR you mentioned pointing out likely what's happening. I think the fix might be to put parentheses around the new conditions added in the pr

```python
and (line_info.raw_the_rest.startswith(" ")
    or not line_info.raw_the_rest.strip()) 
```
